title: Isomorphism on two terms of a distinguished triangle
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] and let $\Phi,\Psi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be exact functors with their natural shift isomorphisms $\varphi_X:\Phi(X[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi(X)[1]$ and $\psi_X:\Psi(X[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi(X)[1]$. Let $\alpha:\Phi\to\Psi$ be a natural transformation compatible with these isomorphisms: $\psi_X\circ\alpha_{X[1]}=\alpha_X[1]\circ\varphi_X$ for every $X$. For every distinguished triangle $T=(X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1])$ [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift], if any two of $\alpha_X,\alpha_Y,\alpha_Z$ are isomorphisms, then the third is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix such a distinguished triangle $T$. Its image triangles have vertices $(\Phi X,\Phi Y,\Phi Z)$ and $(\Psi X,\Psi Y,\Psi Z)$, arrows $(\Phi u,\Phi v,\varphi_X\circ\Phi w)$ and $(\Psi u,\Psi v,\psi_X\circ\Psi w)$, respectively. Both image triangles are distinguished, by the definition of exact functor. This checks the distinguishedness hypotheses needed below.

source.place: Functor.mapTriangle, lines 42--53; Functor.IsTriangulated and map_distinguished, lines 186--191 (exact functor; Stacks Tag 014V)

proof.text:
Apply the shift-compatible-transformation lemma to obtain the morphism $a=(\alpha_X,\alpha_Y,\alpha_Z):\Phi T\to\Psi T$. Its first two squares are naturality for $u$ and $v$. Explicitly its last square is
$$\alpha_X[1]\circ\varphi_X\circ\Phi(w)=\psi_X\circ\alpha_{X[1]}\circ\Phi(w)=\psi_X\circ\Psi(w)\circ\alpha_Z.$$
The first equality is the stated shift compatibility at $X$ and the second is naturality for $w$. Thus the cited lemma is used for precisely its assertion about the three components forming a morphism of image triangles; distinguishedness comes from Step 1.

source.place: CategoryTheory.NatTrans.mapTriangle, lines 36--45; the morphism-of-triangles definition is Stacks Tag 0144

proof.text: Apply the two-out-of-three lemma to $a$ and the two distinguished image triangles. Its hypotheses hold in $\mathcal D$, which is in particular pre-triangulated. If $(\alpha_X,\alpha_Y)$ are isomorphisms, its third-component assertion gives that $\alpha_Z$ is an isomorphism. If $(\alpha_X,\alpha_Z)$ are isomorphisms, its second-component assertion gives that $\alpha_Y$ is an isomorphism. If $(\alpha_Y,\alpha_Z)$ are isomorphisms, its first-component assertion gives that $\alpha_X$ is an isomorphism. These are all possible pairs, proving the claim.

source.place: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.isIso₂_of_isIso₁₃, lines 479--507; isIso₃_of_isIso₁₂, lines 516--519; isIso₁_of_isIso₂₃, lines 526--529; Stacks Tag 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle)

split_report.summary: Corrected the missing compatibility of the natural transformation with the exact functors’ shift isomorphisms, with a counterexample in report.md. Made explicit that both image triangles are distinguished by exactness and checked the third commuting square. Applied the existing generic triangle-morphism Mathlib leaf to all three pairs of vertices. No new nodes and no attachment claim. Removed the unused six-functor context preamble and its statement dependency so the categorical assertion introduces all its objects and hypotheses on its own.
split_report.blueprint: The node's imported paragraph and the triangle part of unit sk-lem-sf-determination step 1 intend the five-lemma argument on a map of distinguished triangles. Their inference that mere naturality and functor exactness give that map is false: in D^b(fdVect_k), the natural endomorphism of Id acting as identity on H^0 and zero on other cohomological degrees has components (id,0,0) on the distinguished triangle k[0]→0→k[1]→k[1], so the first two are invertible and the third is not. The corrected statement adds exactly the missing shift-compatibility equation. Step 1 forms the distinguished images, Step 2 checks all three squares, and Step 3 invokes the categorical five lemma (Stacks 014A). For general triangulated categories no conservative family H^q is part of the hypotheses; the generic triangle-morphism theorem realizes the intended five-lemma argument without adding that extra structure. The imported phrase 'a morphism whose cone has vanishing cohomology is zero' must mean that the cone is zero and the morphism is an isomorphism in the derived-category case. The unit record is not changed: this node is only its triangle clause, not its key statement; the omitted shift-compatibility premise is reported for the unit and its callers.

They hold already for pretriangulated categories, hence apply to the node’s triangulated categories without using the octahedral axioms. Functor.CommShift and Functor.IsTriangulated encode the given shift isomorphisms and exactness; NatTrans.CommShift encodes compatibility, whose degree-one equation is precisely the node’s equation. For coherent integer shifts, the degree-one equation extends to all integers by iteration and inverse shift. No replacement module or duplicate statement is added.
